title: Finite-free scalar extension commutes with completion and its unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $a:R\to S$ a map of sheaves of commutative rings. Assume $S$ is finite free as an $R$-module sheaf, meaning $S\cong R^{\oplus d}$ for some finite $d$. Use the module derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $C(M)=M\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and the canonical Koszul completion reflectors with their units [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector]. Let $t$ be a global section of $R$, let $v$ be a global section of $S$, and suppose $a(t)=wv^e$ with $w$ a global unit of $S$ and $e\geq1$. Write $\Lambda_{R,t}$ and $\Lambda_{S,v}$ for these reflectors, with units $\eta^R,\eta^S$.

There is a canonical natural isomorphism in $D(S)$
$$\kappa_M:C\Lambda_{R,t}M\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{S,v}CM,\qquad \kappa_M\,C(\eta^R_M)=\eta^S_{CM}.$$
In particular $C$ carries locally derived $t$-complete objects to locally derived $v$-complete objects. The isomorphism is independent of a basis. It commutes with the canonical cochain shifts. For the identity coefficient map and $v=t$ it is the tensor-unit comparison. For a tower of finite-free ring-sheaf maps for which each preceding parameter is a unit times a positive power of the next, successive $\kappa$'s agree with the direct $\kappa$ under balanced derived tensor associativity.

proof.text: For every specified Koszul limit presentation, compare with the same augmented Cech Hom functor. Compose the inverse comparison for the reflector presentation with the comparison for the given presentation. Its unit equation transports complete outputs, the Hom bijection and the invertible-unit criterion to the actual presentation. Naturality and both idempotence isomorphisms also transport from Cech completion.

proof.text: Use finite-free strict tower transport only for exactness of ordinary scalar extension. The unique ordinary left-adjoint comparison transfers exactness to the tensor functor in the flat scalar Koszul comparison. Its unit-normalized restriction comparison, together with conservativity of exact derived restriction, identifies t-completeness of a restricted object with a(t)-completeness over S. The unit-power theorem identifies the latter with v-completeness. Conservativity here is the unconditional helper of the flat ringed ideal equivalence module; no quotient-isomorphism hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Instantiate the existing normalized closed tensor structures and the scalar tensor comparison for the given universal scalar model. The finite-free coordinate theorem supplies X^d isomorphic to the restriction of scalar extension of X. Completeness is a strictly full triangulated property, hence is closed under finite products, and the finite biproduct is such a product. Therefore scalar extension preserves completeness, also for d=0. Only the existing basis isomorphism a_Q is used; no internal-Hom base-change conclusion is assumed.

proof.text: For complete Y the scalar adjunction transports the reflector Hom bijection to bijectivity of precomposition with C(eta_R): Hom(C Lambda_R X,Y) to Hom(CX,Y). Both C Lambda_R X and Lambda_S CX are complete. Extend eta_S across C(eta_R), and extend C(eta_R) across eta_S. The two bijections prove the resulting maps inverse. Injectivity proves their naturality and uniqueness, yielding the asserted unique normalized natural isomorphism. Completeness preservation is the finite-biproduct argument of the preceding step.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; finite-free scalar change and its unit/shift/tower normalization extracted from the retained scalar-extension proof steps 6-7 (agent lemma).

proof.text: For coherence, conjugate precomposition with C(eta_R) by the normalized comparison. Idempotence and naturality of the S-unit imply injectivity into any target whose S-unit is invertible. Its unit is invertible on completed objects; the given unit-compatible shift structure makes it invertible on every shift. The shift square follows by this cancellation, scalar-shift naturality, and the two normalized unit equations.

source.place: Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul; finite-free scalar change and its unit/shift/tower normalization extracted from the retained scalar-extension proof steps 6-7 (agent lemma).

proof.text: For identity scalars, naturality of the actual scalar unitor and completion unit makes the proposed tensor-unit map normalized. For two scalar maps, naturality of the balanced derived associator, successive normalization and target-unit naturality make the successive and direct comparisons have the same precomposition. Transport cancellation by the associator and cancel as in the preceding step. This proves the unchanged identity and composition equations.
